module_title: Forest Types - Rainfall Ranges and Key Species
introduction: At this level, we categorize the forests precisely by their annual rainfall requirements and memorize the specific, economically important tree species associated with each ecosystem.

core_concepts.title: Rainfall Requirements
core_concepts.description: Evergreen: > 200 cm. Moist Deciduous: 100 to 200 cm. Dry Deciduous: 70 to 100 cm. Thorn Forests: < 70 cm.

core_concepts.title: Trees of Evergreen Forests
core_concepts.description: Found in Western Ghats, Andaman & Nicobar, and Northeast India. Important trees: Mahogany, Ebony, Rosewood, and Rubber.

core_concepts.title: Trees of Deciduous Forests
core_concepts.description: Teak is the most dominant species of the moist deciduous forest. Other key trees: Sal, Shisham, Sandalwood (Chandan), Peepal, and Neem.

core_concepts.title: Montane Forests (Mountain Vegetation)
core_concepts.description: In mountainous areas, the decrease in temperature with increasing altitude leads to a change in vegetation. It transitions from tropical to subtropical, then to coniferous trees (Pine, Deodar, Cedar), and finally to alpine vegetation.

important_entities.name: Sandalwood (Chandan)
important_entities.significance: Sandalwood is a highly valuable, fragrant wood predominantly found in the dry deciduous forests of the Deccan plateau, specifically in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners love to mix up tree species. Remember: Teak and Sal shed their leaves (Deciduous). Mahogany, Ebony, and Rosewood do NOT shed their leaves simultaneously (Evergreen).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Rosewood, Ebony, Evergreen, Mahogany. Use this to instantly filter out deciduous options in multiple-choice questions.

exam_strategy_tips: Rainfall matching questions are incredibly common. Lock in the 200cm, 100-200cm, and <70cm thresholds in your memory.
If a question asks which tree species is commercially the most important in India, the answer is 'Teak'.
